subjects.name: Lionel Messi
clues: As a boy he needed hormone treatment because he was growing too slowly.
At 13 he left Rosario for Spain to join a famous club's youth academy.
By 2023 he had won a record eight Ballon d'Or awards.
In 2023 he moved to the United States to play for Inter Miami.
He captained Argentina to victory at the 2022 World Cup in Qatar.
subjects.fact: Barcelona's first offer to him was famously written on a paper napkin in 2000.

subjects.name: Cristiano Ronaldo
clues: Born on the island of Madeira in 1985, he was named partly after a US president.
He left Sporting Lisbon for Manchester United as a teenager in 2003.
He became Real Madrid's all-time top goalscorer.
He led Portugal to its first major trophy at Euro 2016.
This Portuguese superstar celebrates goals with a leap and a loud 'Siu!'
subjects.fact: In 2022 he became the first man to score at five different World Cups.

subjects.name: Pelé
clues: He picked up his famous nickname as a schoolboy and at first disliked it.
He spent most of his career at Santos before ending it with the New York Cosmos.
At just 17 he scored twice in a World Cup final in Sweden.
He is the only player to win the World Cup three times: 1958, 1962 and 1970.
Brazil's legendary number 10, often called simply 'The King' of football.
subjects.fact: He claimed more than 1,000 career goals when friendly matches are counted.

subjects.name: Diego Maradona
clues: He grew up in a poor neighbourhood on the edge of Buenos Aires.
He became a hero in southern Italy after leading Napoli to the 1987 league title.
In a 1986 match against England he scored the 'Goal of the Century'.
In that same game he also scored the famous 'Hand of God' goal.
He captained Argentina to World Cup glory in Mexico in 1986.
subjects.fact: In 2020 Napoli renamed its stadium after him.

subjects.name: Zinedine Zidane
clues: The son of Algerian immigrants, he grew up in a tough district of Marseille.
He was famous for an elegant spinning move to glide past defenders.
He scored two headers in the 1998 World Cup final against Brazil.
As Real Madrid's coach he won three Champions League titles in a row (2016-2018).
The bald French playmaker known to fans as 'Zizou'.
subjects.fact: His left-foot volley won the 2002 Champions League final in Glasgow.

subjects.name: Johan Cruyff
clues: He grew up in Amsterdam, close to the stadium of the club he made famous.
He won three European Cups in a row with Ajax from 1971 to 1973.
A trick where the ball is dragged behind the standing leg is named after him.
He led the Netherlands to the 1974 World Cup final playing 'Total Football'.
As Barcelona coach he built the 'Dream Team' that won the 1992 European Cup.
subjects.fact: He won the Ballon d'Or three times, in 1971, 1973 and 1974.

subjects.name: Kylian Mbappé
clues: He grew up in Bondy, a suburb just outside Paris.
As a teenager he won the French league title with Monaco in 2017.
At 19 he scored in a World Cup final, the first teenager to do so since Pelé.
He scored a hat-trick in the 2022 World Cup final but ended up on the losing side.
This speedy French forward joined Real Madrid in 2024 from Paris Saint-Germain.
subjects.fact: He won the World Cup with France in 2018.

subjects.name: David Beckham
clues: Born in east London in 1975, he grew up a fan of the club he later starred for.
In 1996 he famously scored from inside his own half.
He was part of Manchester United's treble-winning team of 1999.
In 2007 he moved to LA Galaxy, and he later co-founded Inter Miami.
England's former captain, famed for curling free kicks and married to a Spice Girl.
subjects.fact: The 2002 film Bend It Like Beckham was named after his curling free kicks.

subjects.name: Michael Jordan
clues: As a high school sophomore he missed out on a place in his school's top team.
His late shot won North Carolina the 1982 college championship.
In 1994 he briefly swapped his sport for minor-league baseball.
He won six NBA titles with the Chicago Bulls in the 1990s.
Wearing number 23, he inspired Nike's famous 'Air' line of sneakers.

links.name: Nike
links.rel: has a famous shoe line with

subjects.fact: He won two Olympic gold medals, in 1984 and with the 1992 'Dream Team'.

subjects.name: LeBron James
clues: Born in Akron, Ohio, he was on a magazine cover while still in high school.
He was the first pick of the 2003 NBA draft, chosen by his home-state team.
He won NBA titles with Miami, Cleveland and Los Angeles.
In 2023 he passed Kareem Abdul-Jabbar to become the NBA's all-time top scorer.
The basketball superstar nicknamed 'King' who played alongside his son Bronny.
subjects.fact: In 2016 he led Cleveland back from 3-1 down in the NBA Finals.

subjects.name: Kobe Bryant
clues: He spent part of his childhood in Italy, where his father played basketball.
He went straight from high school to the NBA in 1996.
He played all 20 of his seasons for one team, winning five titles.
In 2006 he scored 81 points in a single game, the second-most ever.
The Lakers legend nicknamed 'Black Mamba', who wore numbers 8 and 24.
subjects.fact: He won an Academy Award for the animated short film Dear Basketball.

subjects.name: Stephen Curry
clues: His father Dell was also an NBA player, known for sharp shooting.
Few big colleges wanted him, so he starred at little Davidson College.
In 2016 he became the first unanimous choice for NBA Most Valuable Player.
He won four NBA titles with the Golden State Warriors between 2015 and 2022.
The point guard who transformed basketball with long-range three-point shooting.

links.name: LeBron James
links.rel: met in four straight NBA Finals

subjects.fact: He and LeBron James were both born in the same hospital in Akron, Ohio.

subjects.name: Roger Federer
clues: As a boy he worked as a ball boy at the tournament in his hometown of Basel.
His first Grand Slam title came on grass in London in 2003.
By his retirement in 2022 he had won a record eight Wimbledon singles titles.
His long rivalry with Rafael Nadal is one of the greatest in sport.
The elegant Swiss tennis star famous for his one-handed backhand.
subjects.fact: He won 20 Grand Slam singles titles in his career.

subjects.name: Serena Williams
clues: She learned the game on public courts in Compton, California, coached by her father.
She won her first Grand Slam title at the 1999 US Open, aged 17.
She won the 2017 Australian Open while pregnant.
Her 23 Grand Slam singles titles are the Open Era record for women.
She often teamed up in doubles with her older sister Venus.
subjects.fact: She and her sister Venus won 14 Grand Slam doubles titles together.

subjects.name: Rafael Nadal
clues: Born on Mallorca in 1986, he was coached for years by his uncle Toni.
Though he writes with his right hand, he plays tennis left-handed.
He beat Roger Federer in the 2008 Wimbledon final, often called the greatest match.
He won the French Open a record 14 times.
The Spanish 'King of Clay' who liked to bite his trophies for the cameras.
subjects.fact: He retired in 2024 with 22 Grand Slam singles titles.

subjects.name: Novak Djokovic
clues: He grew up in Belgrade and first picked up a racket at the age of four.
He won his first Grand Slam title at the 2008 Australian Open.
By 2023 he had won the Australian Open a record ten times.
He won Olympic gold in men's singles at the Paris 2024 Games.
The Serbian star who reached 24 Grand Slam singles titles in 2023.
subjects.fact: He has spent more weeks ranked world number one than any other player.

subjects.name: Ayrton Senna
clues: He began racing in São Paulo after his father built him a go-kart at age four.
He was famously brilliant in the rain, as he showed at Monaco in 1984.
His fierce rivalry with teammate Alain Prost defined McLaren in the late 1980s.
He won three Formula One world titles: 1988, 1990 and 1991.
The Brazilian legend who won the Monaco Grand Prix a record six times.
subjects.fact: He won 41 Formula One Grand Prix races in his career.

subjects.name: Michael Schumacher
clues: He grew up at a go-kart track in Kerpen, where his father worked.
He won his first two world titles with Benetton in 1994 and 1995.
He won five world titles in a row with Ferrari from 2000 to 2004.
His record of seven Formula One titles was later matched by Lewis Hamilton.
The German driver who brought Ferrari back to glory.
subjects.fact: His son Mick also raced in Formula One.

subjects.name: Lewis Hamilton
clues: He grew up in Stevenage and first showed his talent racing remote-control cars.
At ten he told McLaren's boss that he wanted to race for him one day.
In 2008 he became the youngest world champion at the time, aged 23.
He won six of his seven world titles with Mercedes.
The British driver who joined Ferrari in 2025 after 12 seasons at Mercedes.
subjects.fact: He was knighted in 2021 for services to motorsport.

subjects.name: Max Verstappen
clues: Both his parents raced: his father in Formula One, his mother in karting.
He made his Formula One debut at 17, before he had a road driving licence.
At 18 he became the youngest Grand Prix winner, in Spain in 2016.
He won his first world title in a dramatic final race in Abu Dhabi in 2021.
The Dutch Red Bull driver who won four straight titles from 2021 to 2024.
subjects.fact: He won 19 of the 22 races in the 2023 season.

subjects.name: Muhammad Ali
clues: He took up boxing at 12 after his bicycle was stolen in Louisville, Kentucky.
He won Olympic light-heavyweight gold in Rome in 1960.
He fought Joe Frazier in the 'Fight of the Century' and the 'Thrilla in Manila'.
He beat George Foreman in Zaire in the 1974 'Rumble in the Jungle'.
The heavyweight who could 'float like a butterfly, sting like a bee'.
subjects.fact: He lit the Olympic cauldron at the 1996 Atlanta Games.

subjects.name: Mike Tyson
clues: He grew up in Brooklyn and was trained as a teenager by Cus D'Amato.
He was known for his 'peek-a-boo' style and fearsome early knockouts.
In 1986, aged 20, he became the youngest heavyweight champion ever.
He lost his title in a huge upset to Buster Douglas in Tokyo in 1990.
The heavyweight with a face tattoo who had a cameo in the comedy The Hangover.
subjects.fact: He is a keen pigeon keeper, a hobby he started as a boy in Brooklyn.

subjects.name: Manny Pacquiao
clues: He grew up in poverty in the southern Philippines and left home as a teenager.
He is the only boxer to win world titles in eight weight divisions.
He fought Floyd Mayweather in 2015 in one of the richest bouts ever.
Away from the ring he served as a senator in his home country.
The Filipino southpaw nicknamed 'PacMan'.
subjects.fact: He has also played professional basketball and recorded songs.

subjects.name: Floyd Mayweather
clues: Born in Grand Rapids, Michigan, he came from a family of boxers.
He won a bronze medal at the 1996 Atlanta Olympics.
He beat Manny Pacquiao in 2015 and UFC star Conor McGregor in 2017.
He retired with a perfect professional record of 50 wins and no defeats.
The defensive genius nicknamed 'Money', famous for showing off his wealth.
subjects.fact: His father and two uncles were also professional boxers.

subjects.name: Sachin Tendulkar
clues: He made his Test debut at just 16, against Pakistan in 1989.
In 2010 he hit the first double century in a men's one-day international.
He was the first player to score 100 international centuries.
He won the World Cup at his home stadium in Mumbai in 2011.
India's 'Little Master', who played a record 200 Test matches.
subjects.fact: He became the first sportsperson to receive India's highest civilian award, the Bharat Ratna.

subjects.name: Don Bradman
clues: As a boy he practised alone, hitting a golf ball against a water tank with a stump.
England's 'Bodyline' bowling of 1932-33 was designed mainly to stop him.
He needed just four runs in his final innings to average 100, but was out for nought.
His Test batting average of 99.94 is the highest in history.
Australia's greatest batsman, knighted in 1949.
subjects.fact: The address of the Australian Broadcasting Corporation's postal box was set at 9994 in his honour.

subjects.name: Virat Kohli
clues: He captained his country to victory at the Under-19 World Cup in 2008.
He was named player of the match in the final of the 2024 T20 World Cup.
By 2023 he had made a world-record 50 centuries in one-day internationals.
In 2025 he finally won the IPL with Royal Challengers Bengaluru.
The former India captain from Delhi, married to actress Anushka Sharma.

links.name: Sachin Tendulkar
links.rel: broke a one-day century record of

subjects.fact: He played his entire IPL career for one team, from the first season in 2008.

subjects.name: Brian Lara
clues: He grew up in Trinidad, the tenth of eleven children.
In 1994 he scored 501 not out for Warwickshire, a first-class record.
Also in 1994 he made 375 against England, then the Test record.
He took back the Test record in 2004 with 400 not out against England.
The West Indies left-hander nicknamed 'The Prince of Port of Spain'.
subjects.fact: His 400 not out is still the highest individual score in Test cricket.

subjects.name: Usain Bolt
clues: As a boy in rural Jamaica he loved cricket and football more than running.
At 15 he won the 200 m at the 2002 World Junior Championships in Kingston.
He won both the 100 m and 200 m at three straight Olympics, from 2008 to 2016.
He ran the 100 m in a world-record 9.58 seconds in Berlin in 2009.
The Jamaican sprinter famous for his sky-pointing archer pose.
subjects.fact: He also set the 200 m world record, 19.19 seconds, in Berlin in 2009.

subjects.name: Jesse Owens
clues: The son of a sharecropper, he moved from Alabama to Cleveland as a boy.
In 1935 he set three world records and tied a fourth in under an hour.
His friendship with German long-jump rival Luz Long became legendary.
He won four gold medals at the 1936 Olympics in Berlin.
The American track star who won 100 m, 200 m, long jump and relay gold in 1936.
subjects.fact: A street beside Berlin's Olympic Stadium is named after him.

subjects.name: Michael Phelps
clues: As a boy in Baltimore he took up swimming partly to burn off extra energy.
He made the US Olympic team at just 15, in 2000.
At the 2008 Beijing Games he won a record eight gold medals.
He won 23 Olympic gold medals in all, by far the most of any athlete.
The American swimmer nicknamed the 'Baltimore Bullet'.
subjects.fact: He won 28 Olympic medals in total, also a record.

subjects.name: Simone Biles
clues: She discovered her sport at age six on a daycare field trip.
She won four gold medals at the 2016 Olympics in Rio de Janeiro.
Several moves are named after her because she was first to do them in competition.
She returned to win three golds at the Paris 2024 Olympics.
The American gymnast who is the most decorated in the sport's history.
subjects.fact: She stands just 1.42 metres tall.

subjects.name: Nadia Comăneci
clues: Coach Béla Károlyi spotted her doing cartwheels in a schoolyard.
She was only 14 when she competed at the 1976 Olympics in Montreal.
The scoreboard showed '1.00' for her famous routine because it could not display her score.
She scored the first perfect 10 in Olympic gymnastics.
The Romanian gymnast who later married American Olympic champion Bart Conner.
subjects.fact: She won three gold medals at the 1976 Games and two more in 1980.

subjects.name: Tiger Woods
clues: At age two he showed off his putting against comedian Bob Hope on a TV show.
In 1997, aged 21, he won the Masters by a record 12 shots.
He held all four major golf titles at the same time in 2000-2001.
In 2019 he won the Masters again after serious back surgery.
The golfer famous for wearing a red shirt on the final day of tournaments.
subjects.fact: His real first name is Eldrick.

subjects.name: Wayne Gretzky
clues: He learned to skate on a backyard rink his father built in Ontario.
He won four Stanley Cups with the Edmonton Oilers in the 1980s.
His 1988 trade to Los Angeles shocked his home country.
When he retired in 1999, the NHL retired his number 99 for every team.
The Canadian ice hockey legend known as 'The Great One'.
subjects.fact: He scored 92 goals in a single season, 1981-82, still the NHL record.

subjects.name: Eliud Kipchoge
clues: As a boy he ran several kilometres to school in Kenya's Nandi County.
At 18 he beat Hicham El Guerrouj to win the 5,000 m world title in 2003.
He won the Olympic marathon in 2016 and again in 2021.
In 2019 in Vienna he ran a marathon in under two hours, in a specially set-up race.
The Kenyan marathon great whose motto is 'No human is limited'.

links.name: Olympic Games
links.rel: won two marathon golds at the

subjects.fact: His sub-two-hour run, 1:59:40, did not count as an official record because of pacers.

subjects.name: Football
clues: Its modern rules were agreed at a meeting in a London tavern in 1863.
Only one player per team may handle the ball, and only inside their own area.
Each side has eleven players and tries to put the ball into the opposing net.
Its biggest tournament, the World Cup, is held every four years.
The world's most popular sport, played by Pelé, Messi and Ronaldo.

links.name: FIFA World Cup
links.rel: has as its biggest tournament the

subjects.fact: A match lasts 90 minutes, in two halves of 45.

subjects.name: Basketball
clues: It was invented in 1891 by a Canadian PE teacher working in Massachusetts.
In the first games the ball had to be fetched out of peach baskets by hand.
Shots from far enough out are worth three points instead of two.
Its top professional league is the NBA, founded in 1946.
The sport of Michael Jordan and LeBron James, with hoops 10 feet high.
subjects.fact: Its inventor, James Naismith, wrote just 13 original rules.

subjects.name: Tennis
clues: Its modern lawn version was patented in England in 1874.
Its scoring goes love, 15, 30, 40, then game.
Its four biggest events each year are known as the Grand Slams.
Players use strung rackets to hit a ball back and forth over a net.
The sport played at Wimbledon by Federer, Nadal and Serena.
subjects.fact: 'Love' for zero may come from the idea of playing for love of the game.

subjects.name: Cricket
clues: Its longest form lasts up to five days and can still end in a draw.
A batter can be given out 'leg before wicket'.
Bowlers aim at three stumps topped by two small bails.
Teams of eleven play Tests, one-day games and short Twenty20 matches.
The bat-and-ball sport adored in India and England, played by Sachin Tendulkar.
subjects.fact: The Ashes series between England and Australia began in 1882.

subjects.name: Chess
clues: Its ancestor, chaturanga, arose in India around the 6th century.
Its queen became the most powerful piece only in the late 1400s.
In 1997 IBM's computer Deep Blue beat the world champion at it.
A pawn that reaches the far side of the board can be promoted.
The game of kings, rooks and bishops, won by checkmate.
subjects.fact: The word 'checkmate' comes from Persian, meaning 'the king is helpless'.

subjects.name: Go
clues: Invented in China over 2,500 years ago, it is among the oldest board games still played.
Players take turns placing black and white stones on the points of a grid.
The standard board has 19 by 19 lines.
Stones are captured by surrounding them, and the aim is to control the most territory.
In 2016 Google DeepMind's AlphaGo program beat top player Lee Sedol at it.
subjects.fact: It has more possible board positions than there are atoms in the observable universe.

subjects.name: Monopoly
clues: It grew out of 'The Landlord's Game', designed by Lizzie Magie in 1904.
Parker Brothers began selling it in 1935.
The streets on the classic US board come from Atlantic City, New Jersey.
Its playing pieces have included a top hat, a racing car and a Scottie dog.
The property-trading game where you collect money for passing Go.

links.name: London
links.rel: has a famous edition set in

subjects.fact: In World War II, special editions helped smuggle escape maps to prisoners of war.

subjects.name: Scrabble
clues: An out-of-work architect, Alfred Butts, invented it during the Great Depression.
He set the letter values by counting letters on newspaper front pages.
Players draw seven letter tiles at a time from a bag.
In the English version, Q and Z are each worth ten points.
The crossword board game with bonus triple-word-score squares.
subjects.fact: The English set has 100 tiles, including two blanks.

subjects.name: Olympic Games
clues: The ancient version was held in honour of Zeus for more than a thousand years.
Pierre de Coubertin revived it, and the first modern edition was held in Athens in 1896.
A flame lit in Greece is carried by torch relay to each host city.
Winners receive gold medals, while second and third get silver and bronze.
The world's biggest multi-sport event, whose flag shows five interlocking rings.
subjects.fact: The five rings stand for the five inhabited continents united by sport.

subjects.name: FIFA World Cup
clues: The first edition was held in Uruguay in 1930, and the hosts won.
By 2022 Brazil had won it a record five times.
Its current trophy, introduced in 1974, shows two figures holding up a globe.
The 2026 edition, in the US, Canada and Mexico, was the first with 48 teams.
Football's biggest tournament, won by Argentina in Qatar in 2022.

links.name: Uruguay
links.rel: was first hosted and won by

subjects.fact: It is held every four years; the only gaps were in 1942 and 1946.

subjects.name: Wimbledon
clues: First held in 1877, it is the oldest tournament of its sport in the world.
Players must wear almost entirely white clothing.
Fans traditionally eat strawberries and cream there.
It is the only Grand Slam tennis event still played on grass.
The tennis championship held each summer at the All England Club in London.
subjects.fact: Around 200,000 portions of strawberries and cream are eaten there each year.

subjects.name: Tour de France
clues: First held in 1903, it was created to boost sales of a sports newspaper.
Its overall leader wears a yellow jersey.
The best climber wears a white jersey with red polka dots.
It lasts about three weeks and crosses the Alps and the Pyrenees.
The world's most famous cycling race, which traditionally finishes in Paris.
subjects.fact: The yellow jersey matches the colour of the paper the original newspaper was printed on.

subjects.name: Real Madrid
clues: Founded in 1902, the club was given a royal title by King Alfonso XIII in 1920.
It plays its home games at the Santiago Bernabéu stadium.
It won the first five European Cups, from 1956 to 1960.
By 2024 it had won the European Cup or Champions League a record 15 times.
The Spanish capital's all-white football giant, nicknamed 'Los Blancos'.
subjects.fact: Its matches against Barcelona are known as 'El Clásico'.

subjects.name: FC Barcelona
clues: It was founded in 1899 by a group led by Swiss businessman Joan Gamper.
Its motto means 'More than a club' in Catalan.
Its home ground, Camp Nou, is one of the largest stadiums in Europe.
Lionel Messi spent over 20 years there, from youth player to superstar.
The blue-and-maroon giant of Catalonia, eternal rival of Real Madrid.
subjects.fact: It is owned by its members, who elect the club president.

subjects.name: Manchester United
clues: It was founded in 1878 as Newton Heath, a team of railway workers.
Its stadium, Old Trafford, is nicknamed 'The Theatre of Dreams'.
Under Sir Alex Ferguson it won 13 English league titles.
In 1999 it won the treble, with two late goals in the Champions League final.
The English football giant nicknamed the 'Red Devils'.
subjects.fact: It won its first European Cup in 1968, ten years after the Munich air disaster.

subjects.name: Los Angeles Lakers
clues: The team started out in Minneapolis, which explains its name.
Its players wear purple and gold.
Magic Johnson and Kareem Abdul-Jabbar led its 'Showtime' teams of the 1980s.
Kobe Bryant and Shaquille O'Neal won three straight titles there from 2000 to 2002.
The Hollywood-area basketball team that LeBron James joined in 2018.
subjects.fact: It moved from Minneapolis, the 'Land of 10,000 Lakes', to California in 1960.
